From live-stream hypothesis
to a creator monetisation
platform

We set out to validate live streaming as a fashion sales channel during the COVID-19 shopping shift. After 50+ interviews, 8,000+ survey responses, and deep co-creation with 150+ content creators, the real opportunity emerged — and we pivoted to build something far more impactful.

My Role
Lead Researcher, Service Designer & UX/UI
Team
UX design team + multi-stakeholder workshops
Methods
Interviews, surveys, service blueprint, concept testing, usability testing
Outcome
Strategic pivot + full product launch with affiliate commerce model

Background

Live-stream shopping was booming across Asia. We needed to understand why.

During COVID-19, shopping habits shifted dramatically. Live-stream commerce exploded across Asia, attracting major startup investment. Our mission was to understand the landscape, validate emerging opportunities, and determine whether live streaming could become a viable sales channel for independent fashion brands — or if a bigger opportunity was hiding underneath.

Starting hypothesis
Live streaming is an untapped sales channel for independent fashion brands that could rival established platforms like ASOS or Shopify.
Core questions
Do shoppers prefer indie brands over labels? Does live video influence purchase decisions? Who and what shapes buying behaviour?

Phase 1 — Discovery

Understanding the landscape: users, behaviours & the competitive market

I led recruitment and initial research, engaging startup founders, sellers, buyers, and brand owners through prototype testing and structured interviews. We mapped the user ecosystem across four distinct personas and built a value proposition canvas to identify where the real product-market fit could lie.

Research Artifacts

Research participant recruiting, screener & discussion guides, target audience personas, and value proposition canvas

Key findings from Phase 1
Growing appetite for indie brands — shoppers showed strong preference for independent, niche fashion over mainstream labels, driven by values alignment and uniqueness
Trust is the live-stream variable — live streaming can influence purchase decisions, but only when the host has genuine credibility and an established audience relationship
Target buyer profile — female shoppers 25–40, city-based, values-conscious, wants discovery and inspiration, frustrated by inability to find relevant independent products

Phase 2 — Journey Mapping

Tracing the full path from inspiration to purchase — and finding where it breaks

We explored how fashion stylists recommend outfits, how creators pick and present products, and how consumers actually discover and shop online. We mapped best and worst experiences, platform choices, and typical purchase categories — and identified the exact friction points along the discovery-to-purchase journey.

Pain points uncovered along the journey
Unclear sizing & poor return policies — eroded trust before checkout; a primary driver of drop-off for independent brands
Lack of real product context — shoppers couldn't visualise items on themselves or understand how pieces fit their lifestyle without seeing them styled
Fragmented collaboration — no single platform effectively connected brands, stylists, creators, and consumers into a coherent discovery-to-purchase flow
Navigation complexity — existing platforms built for breadth, not curation; shoppers couldn't find niche or value-aligned independent products efficiently

Phase 3 — Large-scale Validation

Testing the live-streaming model at scale — with real creators, brands & shoppers

I guided the UX design team in creating a comprehensive research plan, coordinating collection and synthesis of insights across a diverse set of subject matter experts. We ran structured interviews, workshops, focus groups, and post-launch usability testing across all stakeholder types.

Phase 4 — The Pivot

The data told a different story. We listened.

Across 150+ creator conversations, a consistent pattern emerged. Creators didn't need another live-stream sales channel. Their biggest pain was the fragmented, inefficient journey from creating content to getting paid — managing brand partnerships, tracking commissions, and navigating affiliate admin while trying to produce content.

The insight that changed everything
The real problem wasn't the sales channel —
it was the broken creator-to-payment pipeline.

We saw a bigger opportunity in the creator economy: build a tool that streamlines the entire promotion-to-payment workflow, so creators can focus on what they do best — creating — while monetising their influence with zero friction, zero negotiations, and zero admin overhead.

What we stopped building
Live streaming as the primary feature — it was a means to an end, not the real value creators needed
What we built instead
A style-to-shop creator tool: upload inspo → AI product matching → curated mini shop → automatic affiliate commission

Design Exploration

Iterating on the core creator experience — moodboards, import flows & content customisation

We ran co-creation workshops with the same creators who participated in earlier research rounds, building and testing the tool together. Key UX challenges included the inspiration import flow, moodboard creation, content customisation for IG Reels and TikTok, and product matching.

Moodboard Import Flow
Moodboard Detail View

Left: 6-version iteration of the inspiration import flow (Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok, device). Right: Moodboard detail with creator profile branding and shoppable product links

Content Customiser — Canvas Editor
Customiser Iterations & Add Details

Canvas-based IG Reel & TikTok editor with background swap, drag/drop, text controls — 10+ iterations. Right: Onboarding tooltips and moodboard details flow

Key UX decisions made through iteration
Import source choice upfront — giving creators control over where inspiration comes from (Instagram, Pinterest, TikTok, device) reduced friction at the first step
Canvas-first editing — a freeform drag/drop canvas for IG Reel and TikTok format gave creators flexibility without complexity; contextual tooltips guided first-time use
Save draft before publish — allowing creators to save work mid-session dramatically reduced abandonment during the creation flow
Moodboard detail = creator brand — the moodboard view doubles as a creator profile page, reinforcing their personal brand alongside shoppable product links

Commerce Design

End-to-end shopping experience — from product discovery to payment

Alongside the creator tool, we designed a full commerce experience for buyers — covering product discovery, detailed product pages, cart management, checkout, order tracking, and payment methods designed for global markets.

Commerce Screens

Product detail page, cart, checkout with token rewards system, order management (in-progress / delivered / cancelled), and payment methods

CreatorShop & Discovery Feed

Alloshop CreatorShop landing page, moodboard home with insights, moodboard feed from creators, and creator profile with shop tab (86 products)

Notable commerce design decisions
Token reward system — "Earn 1,413 tokens after this purchase" gamifies loyalty and encourages repeat engagement without a traditional points programme UI
Creator attribution on product pages — every product links back to the creator whose moodboard featured it, reinforcing the trust loop between creator and buyer
Buy Now Pay Later (Klarna) — added to reduce price sensitivity for higher-value independent brand items; key for the 25-40 demographic
Back to Moodboard Shop CTA — post-purchase, buyers are routed back to the creator's shop, not a generic homepage, maintaining the creator commerce loop

Final Design

The product — style-driven creator commerce, end to end

The final Alloshop platform brings together a creator-centric moodboard tool, AI-powered product matching from 1,000+ brands, a personal mini shop, and automatic commission tracking — all in one seamless mobile experience. No brand negotiations. No spreadsheets. No chasing payments.
